paths_reviewed.review_notes: Static review: the scan walks the configured roots and reports files by relative path, size, timestamp, class, protection and expiry/quota. It contains no delete/apply operation; the only writeFileSync is optional report output. Policy root paths are resolved without a relative-path containment check; a symlink in a managed-root position can be traversed. Scan errors are recorded on the report, but runCli has no nonzero-on-errors behavior. --policy may select a custom policy, while report.policy.path is always the default policy path.

Three Node test cases cover policy schema/default classes, expired unprotected candidate selection with active/unknown preservation, and refusal to run without --dry-run plus bounded JSON report output. Fixture creation and report writes are under mkdtemp in /tmp and t.after removes the directory. They do not cover overwrite refusal, symlink/root escape, custom-policy report provenance, or exit behavior when scanning errors occur.

The policy protects legal-hold, active-evidence and unknown classes; generated-run uses 14 days/8 GiB, coverage-run 30 days/12 GiB, and active-evidence has a 64 GiB consultive quota. All seven managed roots are relative, and current lstat observations show each exists as a directory (none is a symlink). ACL profiles are expectations, not applied permissions.

The runbook says candidates are suggestions only, requires owner review and exact authority/recoverability before removal, and expressly leaves external provider retention and destination authorization unproven. It says ACL policy is recorded, not changed by the dry-run.

boundary_review.mutation_boundary: No delete/unlink/rmdir/apply operation exists in the runner. It can write JSON when an explicit --output is given; the current test creates a new file in a temporary fixture only.
boundary_review.policy_alignment: Current policy keeps active evidence, legal-hold and unknown files protected; TTL/quota only selects unprotected candidate records. The Markdown runbook correctly requires owner authorization and recoverability before a separate removal action.
boundary_review.acl_and_external_storage: The program reports ACL profiles but does not inspect or apply actual modes/ACLs, and local execution does not prove provider retention or access control.
boundary_review.no_external_boundary: No database, provider, network, external target, cleanup or report write in the shared repository was exercised.

findings_and_limits.observation: With explicit --output, runCli calls writeFileSync on the resolved caller path without exclusive-create, existence, symlink, containment or protected-evidence checks. It can replace an existing file, including an evidence file; mode 0600 applies only when creating a new file. Current tests write only a new /tmp fixture path.

validatePolicy checks managed_roots is a non-empty array but does not validate each path as relative/canonical or contain it under scanRoot. A symlink used as a managed root is followed by readdirSync. Current shipped roots are relative and all current roots were ordinary directories; a changed policy or explicit root can still scan outside the intended tree and report path metadata.
The CLI supports --policy, but buildDryRunReport always serializes defaultPolicyPath as policy.path, so a report generated from a custom policy can name the wrong policy source.

Unreadable roots/files are summarized in roots.errors and totals.errors, but the CLI does not fail or set a nonzero exit status for an incomplete scan. Automation must inspect the report rather than trust exit status.
ACL profiles are descriptive only; actual filesystem ACLs, workflow retention and provider storage policy are not verified. The runbook states this limitation and requires external owner action.

candidate_actions: Keep this artifact as a static tooling review; do not invoke a cleanup operation or write a report into shared evidence.

Harden policy root containment and symlink-root handling, bind the actual policy path into output, make scan errors fail clearly for automation, and protect existing report targets before using this as release evidence.
Keep external provider retention and any future deletion under owner authority and a separately reviewed recovery plan.
